skill.description: NeuroKit2 guidance for processing physiological signals such as ECG, EEG, EDA, respiration, PPG, EMG, and EOG data.

skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, Python examples, and biomedical terms that resemble reconnaissance keywords. One confirmed issue remains: the skill recommends installing a mutable development zipball from GitHub, which introduces supply chain risk if users run it directly.

remediation.issue: Development install command uses a mutable GitHub zipball URL.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the development install example with a pinned PyPI release, pinned commit archive, or checksum-verified installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Installation commands are shown without warning users about remote code execution risk.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that users should review and pin packages before installing development versions from remote repositories.

content.value_statement: Physiological signal analysis requires many specialized processing steps. This skill guides Claude and Claude Code through NeuroKit2 workflows for ECG, EEG, EDA, respiration, PPG, EMG, EOG, HRV, and event analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guide ECG and PPG processing, peak detection, delineation, and cardiac analysis workflows.
Explain HRV metrics across time, frequency, nonlinear, and respiratory sinus arrhythmia domains.
Support EEG power, microstate, complexity, and source localization workflow selection.
Describe EDA, RSP, EMG, and EOG processing steps with relevant NeuroKit2 functions.
Help combine multiple physiological signals using bio_process and bio_analyze patterns.
Reference detailed method notes for complexity, epochs, events, and general signal processing.
limitations: Does not include raw datasets or validate data quality by itself.
Requires NeuroKit2 and its Python dependencies to be installed separately.
Cannot replace clinical review or domain expert interpretation of physiological signals.
Some advanced EEG workflows may require external libraries such as MNE.

use_cases.title: Process cardiac recordings
use_cases.description: Clean ECG or PPG recordings, detect peaks, and choose HRV analysis methods for study data.

use_cases.title: Prepare multimodal physiology features
use_cases.description: Combine ECG, respiration, EDA, and EMG signals into a unified feature extraction workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan event-related analysis
use_cases.description: Create epochs around experimental events and select NeuroKit2 functions for response summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Start ECG processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me process an ECG recording with NeuroKit2. I have the signal array, sampling rate, and recording duration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose HRV metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend HRV metrics for a five minute resting ECG study and explain which NeuroKit2 functions I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Build multimodal analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a NeuroKit2 workflow for synchronized ECG, EDA, respiration, and EMG signals collected during a stress task.

prompt_templates.title: Audit signal quality and interpretation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned NeuroKit2 analysis for likely signal quality issues, method mismatches, and interpretation limits before I run it.

output_examples.input: I need HRV features from a clean five minute ECG recording.
output: Use ECG processing to identify R peaks.
Run HRV time and frequency methods for standard short-term metrics.
Check peak quality before interpreting autonomic balance.

output_examples.input: I collected EDA during repeated stimulus events.
output: Detect skin conductance responses around each event.
Summarize amplitude, latency, and recovery while noting baseline correction choices.

output_examples.input: I want one workflow for ECG, respiration, and EDA.
output_examples.output: The skill can propose a multimodal NeuroKit2 pipeline that processes each channel, aligns sampling rates, and summarizes combined physiological features.

best_practices: Record and provide the sampling rate, duration, channel names, and sensor type before asking for analysis guidance.
Inspect signal quality and artifact handling before interpreting derived physiological metrics.
Use event-related analysis for short stimulus windows and interval analysis for longer continuous recordings.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret HRV, EEG, or EDA metrics as clinical conclusions without expert review.
Do not mix signals with different sampling rates without documenting resampling and alignment decisions.
Do not install development versions from remote branches unless you pin and verify the source.

faq.question: What signal types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ECG, PPG, EEG, EDA, respiration, EMG, EOG, HRV, epochs, events, and complexity analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill run NeuroKit2 automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and function references. You still need a Python environment with NeuroKit2 installed.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and it can guide local analysis work.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical diagnosis?
faq.answer: No. It can support analysis planning, but clinical interpretation requires qualified professional review.

faq.question: Can it help with multimodal physiology studies?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for processing multiple physiological signals together with NeuroKit2 bio workflows.

faq.question: Why is remote development installation a concern?
faq.answer: A development branch can change over time. Pin releases or commits before installing code from remote repositories.
